findings.title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 4-arg version
findings.body: Ruby has no method overloading. The new `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass a width and a height will now have `max_height` treated as `opts`. That either raises (`opts[:allow_animation]` called on an Integer) or produces a wrong dimensions string. Avatar and thumbnail downsizing elsewhere breaks as a result.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and may not shrink file
findings.body: The return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is ignored. If convert fails, the loop simply retries. After 5 attempts the file can still be over the limit, and the upload proceeds anyway. Resizing to 80% of dimensions also does not guarantee the byte size drops, for example with PNG or with quality changes. Running convert on the same path as both input and output can also corrupt the file on failure.

findings.title: Downsizing uses the tempfile path, whose extension may not match
findings.body: The animated-GIF check uses `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` on the tempfile path. Rack and download tempfiles usually lack the original extension, so animated GIFs are processed by convert using only frame `[0]`. This silently destroys the animation even when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is enabled.

findings.title: Client hardcodes a 10MB limit for all uploads, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb
findings.body: The client-side check previously used `max_<type>_size_kb`. It is now hardcoded to 10MB for attachments as well, so the attachment size setting is no longer enforced or reported on the client. Users get wrong error messages, and the limit mismatches the configured server limit.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download limit for API URL uploads
findings.body: Downloads by URL are now capped at a hardcoded 10MB instead of a setting. Attachments fetched this way bypass the configured limits until `Upload.create_for` runs, and admins cannot tune the cap.
